themes_detail.label: Street Deterioration Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked to 70 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 15.9 per week, a 341% jump (z-score: 6.87), suggesting widespread pavement, pothole, or infrastructure failures affecting multiple blocks in Bed-Stuy.
evidence: 70 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 15.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
341% spike from baseline with z-score of 6.87 (well above statistical significance threshold)
Concurrent spike in lot condition complaints (4 last week vs. 0.2 avg, +1500%) suggests area-wide neglect
reporting_angles: Block-by-block canvass to identify worst-affected streets and document conditions with photos/video
Interview NYCDOT about emergency repair response and budget constraints
Cross-reference with DOB permit data (811 filings) to understand whether construction activity or deferred maintenance is the root cause

themes_detail.label: Noise and Street Disorder Surge
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints jumped to 34 THIS WEEK from a 10.1 weekly average—a 236% spike (z-score: 5.95)—coinciding with elevated dirty condition reports (108 complaints 2 weeks ago, +197%), suggesting a neighborhood-wide disorder or construction-related disruption.
evidence: 34 street/sidewalk noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 10.1 weekly average
Dirty condition spike: 108 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 36.4 weekly average (+197%, z-score: 5.56)
Concurrent abandoned bike complaints (4 last week vs. 0.8 avg, +433%) suggest public space neglect
reporting_angles: Identify whether spike correlates with active construction projects (cross-check 141 new building permits filed)
Interview residents and merchants about noise sources: street vendors, late-night bars, or active demolition/renovation work
Query NYPD noise complaint data to see if enforcement response matches 311 volume

themes_detail.label: Street Sign Infrastructure Failure
themes_detail.summary: Missing street sign complaints exploded to 3 THIS WEEK versus 0.1 weekly average—a 2300% spike (z-score: 8.69, highest severity)—suggesting a systematic or event-driven infrastructure problem affecting neighborhood wayfinding and safety.
evidence: 3 missing street sign complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly baseline—2300% spike
Highest z-score (8.69) in entire spike dataset, indicating extreme outlier status
Potential systemic cause: storm damage, theft, or maintenance contractor negligence
reporting_angles: Physical survey of streets to verify scope and identify which neighborhoods are most affected
Contact NYCDDOT about recent weather events, maintenance schedules, or known sign removal patterns
Determine whether spike is isolated incident or leading indicator of broader street furniture neglect

themes_detail.label: Sanitation and Pest Control Decline
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary conditions jumped 197% (108 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 36.4 avg, z-score: 5.56), while animal-related unsanitary complaints spiked 967% three weeks ago (4 vs. 0.4 avg, z-score: 7.49), signaling a potential pest infestation or waste management breakdown.
evidence: Unsanitary condition complaints: 108 (2 weeks ago) vs. 36.4 weekly average (+197%, z-score: 5.56)
Unsanitary animal/private property complaints: 4 (3 weeks ago) vs. 0.4 weekly average (+967%, z-score: 7.49)
Dirty condition already in top 7 complaint types (560 total over 90 days), indicating chronic baseline
reporting_angles: Investigate whether spike correlates with recent DSNY collection service disruptions or labor issues
Interview Department of Health about rodent/pest trap counts and enforcement data in targeted blocks
Community board budget requests show repeated emphasis on health/safety inspections—determine if staffing limitations are a factor

themes_detail.label: Park and Public Space Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Litter basket requests spiked 500% (6 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.0 avg, z-score: 5.77) and lot condition exploded 1500% (4 last week vs. 0.2 avg, z-score: 5.67), while community board persistently requests new parks and amenities, suggesting urgent infrastructure gaps in public spaces.
evidence: Litter basket requests: 6 (2 weeks ago) vs. 1.0 weekly average (+500%, z-score: 5.77)
Lot condition complaints: 4 (last week) vs. 0.2 weekly average (+1500%, z-score: 5.67)
Community board budget request [01]: 'Provide new or expanded park/amenity' (Department of Parks) appears as recurring ask—indicates chronic unmet demand
reporting_angles: Inventory which specific parks or lots are generating complaints; map against Parks Department capital plan
Interview Parks Commissioner or local elected officials about whether Bed-Stuy has adequate parkland per capita vs. city benchmark
Profile community board's repeated budget requests to show how long residents have been asking for these amenities
